last_commit_bound_phase6_r1_evidence.scope: One bounded synthetic fixture on one real PyTorch/CUDA host and primary GPU; not real-data, scientific, predictive, production, adoption, driver, checkpoint-store, or cross-GPU evidence

last_commit_bound_phase6_r2_evidence.scope: Exact checkpoint recovery for one bounded synthetic fixture on one real PyTorch/CUDA host and primary GPU; the checkpoint existed only in a caller-managed temporary directory, so this is not external-store, real-scheduler-preemption, real-data, production, adoption, or cross-GPU evidence

last_commit_bound_phase6_r3_evidence.scope: Three preregistered bounded synthetic seeds, each repeated in two fresh processes on one real PyTorch/CUDA host, driver, and primary GPU; not real-data, scientific, predictive, production, adoption, or cross-driver/GPU/host evidence

last_commit_bound_phase6_r4_evidence.scope: One bounded synthetic fixture on one real PyTorch/CUDA host and primary GPU. The parent requested termination only after atomic checkpoint and exact child-identity confirmation; this is not involuntary scheduler preemption, real-data, scientific, predictive, production, adoption, or cross-driver/GPU/host evidence

last_commit_bound_phase6_r5_evidence.scope: Two local executions on one bounded synthetic PyTorch/CUDA environment produced public-safe receipts and a single_environment_only comparison. This is trial readiness with zero external receipts, not independent-host, independent-participant, cross-environment portability, real-data, scientific, predictive, production, or adoption evidence.

last_commit_bound_phase6_r6a_evidence.scope: R6A implements a local-only submission and coordinator-attestation protocol over R5 receipts. All participant, receipt, submission, and review fixtures are synthetic; no participant was invited and no external submission was received or accepted. This is protocol readiness, not independent-host, independent-participant, cross-environment portability, real-data, scientific, predictive, production, or adoption evidence.

last_commit_bound_phase7_p7a_evidence.scope: P7A establishes strict candidate-manifest, member-byte closure, source-lifecycle, principal-separation, and explicit-retention ContextBundle engineering contracts with Math/Quant synthetic seam fixtures. It issued no real candidate, closure receipt, ContextBundle, Skill payload, semantic review, installation, activation, or publication evidence; R6B remains frozen with zero external submissions.

cr1.scope: Closes the directly reproducible restricted-content ingress at P7A candidate validation and candidate/context publication without echoing matched values; it is not a complete taint, privacy, retention, encryption, or deletion system.

cr2.scope: Closes deterministic all-CJK and tokenless false similarity with Unicode terms, CJK 2-4 grams, and empty abstention; it does not establish semantic retrieval quality, negative-transfer safety, or promotion validity.

cr4.scope: Separates mandatory evaluation attempts from optional score-bearing results so error, timeout, and inconclusive attempts remain publishable without fabricated output or scores.

cr5.scope: Freezes case-by-seed-by-envelope observations as the comparison unit and keeps metric dimensions separate; it does not establish promotion validity from real candidates or hidden suites.

cr6.scope: Binds the declared evaluation envelope to byte-closed members or resolvable Core artifact pins; hidden dependencies remain attestation-only and no real evaluator or data payload was disclosed.

cr7.scope: Adds fixed Ruff, mypy, and branch-coverage quality gates; these are engineering correctness controls rather than evidence of research validity or external adoption.

cr8.scope: Adds plaintext-free context-material assessment and ContextBundle v2 governance for classification, taint, lifecycle, export, and byte/token preflight; external storage, identity, and semantic review remain declarations.

p7b1.scope: Issues a plaintext-free eligibility preflight with exact candidate, closure, source-case, lineage, criterion, and evidence-byte bindings. eligible_for_payload_drafting is not a Skill payload, semantic review, private evaluation, or promotion decision.

p7b2.scope: Adds a byte-closed synthetic Skill candidate drafting contract with strict UTF-8, restricted-content, minimal frontmatter/layout, DAG, exact eligibility-evidence, and non-negative-size gates. It does not create a real Skill payload or authorize semantic review, private evaluation, promotion, installation, activation, or publication.

p7b3.scope: Adds exact-byte static validation for synthetic Skill candidates, platform metadata, declared trigger/router examples, registry exact collisions, and descriptor diffs. A static pass is not semantic review, real Agent or Router execution, Skill materialization, installation, activation, publication, or promotion.

p7b4.scope: Adds a synthetic semantic-review protocol attestation bound to exact Candidate, P7B3 receipt, review evidence bytes, declared reviewer labels, and seven dimensions. Protocol outcomes do not prove real reviewer identity, independent context, Candidate quality, execution, private evaluation, or promotion.

p7c1.scope: Adds one fail-closed live-execution seam with deterministic in-process and constrained fixed-worker local-process adapters over synthetic Math/Quant fixtures. It reuses existing evaluation and closure records, does not create a duplicate Core schema, and does not prove a sandbox boundary, real Agent or model execution, fresh-session independence, Candidate quality, installation, activation, publication, or promotion.

p7c2.scope: Adds one fail-closed public synthetic suite orchestrator over the existing P7C1 interface and adapters. It preflights the complete case-by-seed grid, preregisters primary and guardrail metrics, freezes a worst-case retry budget, preserves all failed attempts, and assembles the existing suite comparison only for a complete result/run grid. It is not real Agent execution, hidden evaluation, Candidate materialization, fresh-session independence, publication, installation, activation, or promotion.

p7c3.scope: Runs four fresh ephemeral Codex sessions over two public Math cases from one exact archive, with Candidate bytes projected only into repository-external temporary workspaces and runtime-load oracles checked for explicit-load and declared-exclusion behavior. This single-operator provider-unseeded smoke is not independent fresh-session acceptance, statistical Candidate improvement, hidden evaluation, installation, activation, publication, or promotion.

p7d1a.scope: Adds one fail-closed public baseline failure-capture seam with deterministic and Codex CLI adapters. A real run is single-session and zero-retry, and only oracle-proven error plus closed redaction and cleanup may form a qualified failure chain. Synthetic fixtures do not prove a real failure, root cause, reusable Pattern, Candidate quality, or promotion authority.

p7d1b.scope: Adds one fail-closed real Skill Candidate proposal seam with deterministic and Codex CLI adapters. Proposal eligibility requires at least two distinct qualified-failure lineages sharing one reusable Pattern and still passes existing eligibility, bundle, closure, privacy, and cleanup gates. Synthetic fixtures do not create a real Candidate or authorize materialization, review, installation, activation, publication, or promotion.

p7d2.scope: Runs three preregistered public Math baseline calibrations in fixed order from one exact main archive. Every case uses one read-only, no-Web, zero-retry Codex session and an independent exact oracle. All three completed as pass/no_failure, so the adaptive fourth slot and Candidate gate remained closed. This single-operator calibration is not independent acceptance, scientific validation, hidden evaluation, external adoption, or promotion evidence.

p7d3.scope: Runs three preregistered, pairwise nonisomorphic and non-relabelled public line-graph Math calibrations in fixed order from one exact main archive, with independent exact stable-set/monomial/Kostka oracles. Two sessions returned pass/no_failure. One reached the frozen execution timeout and then exposed delayed Windows descendant-pipe cleanup, so it remains capture_inconclusive rather than a model failure. Zero qualified failures kept the adaptive sibling and Candidate gates closed.

p7d3_execution_containment_hardening.scope: Adds one private process-containment module beneath the existing Agent forward-trial interface. POSIX process groups and Windows descendant enumeration plus exact-PID fallback make timeout cleanup, reap, and verification fail closed; cleanup failure remains distinct from timeout and blocks qualified-failure and Candidate-proposal claims. Deterministic Windows/Ubuntu tests are engineering evidence only, not hostile-process isolation, a secure sandbox, Agent quality, scientific validity, hidden evaluation, installation, activation, publication, or promotion.

p7d4.scope: After an initial no-structured-final-output session stopped inconclusive, a newly preregistered compatibility batch ran three fresh public Schur cases plus the first failure's frozen sibling exactly once each. Exact oracles classified all four as graph_structure qualified failures. These single-operator public failures do not establish independent review, Candidate improvement, mathematical novelty, hidden evaluation, or promotion authority.

p7d5.scope: Two failures from distinct public task templates had no collision across independence_group, origin_run_id, dataset_lineage_id, task_template_id, and semantic_duplicate_group and formed one external research-pattern/v1. The one authorized Candidate call was rejected by the contract and was not retried; it generated no Candidate and established no later lifecycle authority.

p7d6.scope: Adds stable sanitized Candidate failure stages/codes and deterministic contract calibration, then records one new-proposal-ID real generator call that produced a byte-closed proposal_ready Candidate. Official skill-creator initialization and quick_validate materialized a deterministic package only outside the repository. Contract, byte closure, materialization, and structural validation do not prove semantic quality, behavioral improvement, independent acceptance, hidden evaluation, installation, activation, publication, or promotion.

boundaries: A manifest hardware declaration is configuration, not an observation.
A Windows or Ubuntu CI job does not prove a GPU or DL framework was present.
Synthetic OOM, NaN, and interrupt injection is engineering evidence, not an observed outage.
FLOP proxy parity is not wall-clock, monetary-cost, memory, or energy parity.
Passed R1-R5 CUDA gates and the R6A compatibility CUDA gate prove only bounded synthetic engineering behavior on the recorded single host, driver observations where recorded, and primary device.
Exact local checkpoint recovery and parent-requested termination do not prove an external store, involuntary scheduler preemption, distributed recovery, or production durability.
Three repeated seeds on one host do not establish portability across drivers, GPUs, hosts, framework versions, or real datasets.
R5 is TRIAL_READY / ZERO_EXTERNAL_RECEIPTS; two local receipts from one normalized environment do not establish independent hosts, participants, portability, or adoption.

R6A is PROTOCOL_READY / ZERO_ACCEPTED_EXTERNAL_SUBMISSIONS; synthetic submission and review fixtures do not establish a real participant, independent host, technical comparison, portability, or adoption.

P7B3 static_pass/static_fail outcomes are synthetic static-contract evidence only; they do not establish semantic correctness, real Router or Agent behavior, Skill materialization, installation, activation, promotion, or publication.

P7B4 is P7B4_SEMANTIC_REVIEW_PROTOCOL_READY / ZERO_REAL_INDEPENDENT_REVIEWS / ZERO_REAL_SKILL_EXECUTIONS / ZERO_PROMOTIONS; synthetic protocol_accept/protocol_reject fixtures and distinct reviewer/session strings do not establish real reviewer identity, context isolation, Candidate quality, or later lifecycle authority.

P7C1 is P7C1_EXECUTION_SEAM_READY / ZERO_REAL_AGENT_EXECUTIONS / ZERO_REAL_INDEPENDENT_REVIEWS / ZERO_PROMOTIONS; deterministic synthetic adapter observations do not establish real Codex/model behavior, a secure sandbox, fresh-session independence, Candidate improvement, or later lifecycle authority.

P7C2 is P7C2_PUBLIC_FORWARD_SUITE_READY / ZERO_REAL_AGENT_EXECUTIONS / ZERO_HIDDEN_EVALUATIONS / ZERO_PROMOTIONS; a complete synthetic case-by-seed grid and public suite comparison do not establish real Candidate execution, independent fresh-session behavior, hidden-suite independence, Candidate improvement, or lifecycle authority.

P7C3 is P7C3_REAL_AGENT_SMOKE_RECORDED / ZERO_INDEPENDENT_FORWARD_ACCEPTANCES / ZERO_HIDDEN_EVALUATIONS / ZERO_PROMOTIONS; four successful ephemeral Codex turns on two public Math cases from one operator do not establish independent acceptance, statistical improvement, hidden-suite independence, research validity, external adoption, or lifecycle authority.

P7D1A/P7D1B are capture/proposal engineering seams: synthetic accepted and rejected fixtures do not establish a real qualified failure, shared reusable mechanism, real Candidate, independent review, installation, activation, or promotion.

P7D2 is P7D2_PUBLIC_BASELINE_CALIBRATION_RECORDED / ZERO_QUALIFIED_FAILURES / ZERO_REAL_CANDIDATES / ZERO_HIDDEN_EVALUATIONS / ZERO_PROMOTIONS; three passing single-operator public Math sessions are calibration evidence only and do not establish independent forward acceptance, scientific validity, external adoption, or lifecycle authority.

P7D4/P7D5 establish bounded single-operator public qualified-failure and Pattern evidence only; same-mechanism exact-oracle failures and five-dimensional lineage separation do not establish independent human or model review, Candidate improvement, mathematical novelty, hidden-suite independence, or promotion authority.
